column1: 1:1|The word of the LORD came to Micah of Moresheth during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah—what he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.|Preserves origin, all three reigns, and both cities as vision scope.

1:2|Hear, all you peoples!
Listen, earth and everything in it!
Let the Lord GOD be a witness against you,
the Lord from his holy temple.|Keeps universal summons, legal witness, and differing divine titles.
1:3|Look, the LORD is coming out of his place.\nHe will come down\nand tread the heights of the earth.|Preserves descent and high places as landscape with cultic resonance.

1:4|The mountains will melt beneath him
and the valleys split apart,
like wax before fire,
like water pouring down a slope.|Keeps both terrain changes and two flowing/melting similes.

1:5|All this is because of Jacob’s rebellion
and the sins of the house of Israel.
What is Jacob’s rebellion? Is it not Samaria?
What are Judah’s high places? Are they not Jerusalem?|Retains the difficult high-places clause and identification of each capital with wrongdoing.

1:6|“I will make Samaria a heap in the open country,
a place for planting vineyards.
I will pour her stones into the valley
and lay her foundations bare.|Preserves agricultural replacement, flowing stones, and exposed foundations.

1:8|Because of this I will lament and wail;
I will go stripped and naked.
I will lament like jackals
and mourn like ostriches.|Keeps the prophet's exposed mourning and both animal cries, with species uncertainty noted if needed.

1:9|Her wound is incurable.
It has reached Judah;
it has touched the gate of my people,
Jerusalem itself.|Makes the geographic progression clear while preserving the feminine wound image.
1:10|Do not tell it in Gath;\ndo not weep at all.\nIn Beth-leaphrah, roll yourself in dust.|Follows read feminine imperative rather than written I rolled; retains place/dust wordplay.

1:11|Pass on, inhabitant of Shaphir,
naked and shamed.
The inhabitant of Zaanan has not come out.
Beth-ezel’s mourning takes away its support from you.|Keeps all three difficult town puns and the obscure support clause without invented geography.
1:12|The inhabitant of Maroth writhes for good,\nfor disaster has come down from the LORD\nto Jerusalem’s gate.|Preserves bitter-town/good tension and explicit divine source of disaster.

1:13|Harness the chariot to the team, inhabitant of Lachish!\nShe was the beginning of sin for daughter Zion,\nfor Israel’s rebellions were found in you.|Keeps horse/Lachish soundplay in note, personified daughter, and accusation without inventing historical details.

1:14|So you will give parting gifts to Moresheth-gath.\nThe houses of Achzib will be a deception\nto the kings of Israel.|Retains parting-gift and false-town wordplay rather than translating names away.
1:15|I will again bring a conqueror to you, inhabitant of Mareshah.\nIsrael’s glory will come to Adullam.|Keeps possessor/Mareshah pun and unexplained glory destination.

1:16|Shave your head and cut off your hair
for the children you cherish.
Make your baldness wide as a vulture’s,
for they have gone into exile away from you.|Uses vulture for baldness context within nesher range and preserves bereavement/exile cause.

2:1|Woe to those who plan wickedness
and devise evil on their beds!
At morning light they carry it out
because the power lies in their hands.|Preserves night planning/morning execution and power rather than mere opportunity.

2:2|They covet fields and seize them,
houses and take them away.
They oppress a man and his household,
a person and his inheritance.|Keeps paired land/house seizures and family inheritance rather than generic greed.

2:3|So this is what the LORD says:
“I am planning disaster against this family,
a yoke you cannot remove from your necks.
You will no longer walk proudly,
for it will be an evil time.|Makes the neck image intelligible with yoke while preserving planning's reversal.

2:4|On that day people will take up a taunt over you
and sing a bitter lament:
‘We are utterly devastated!
He exchanges my people’s portion.
How he takes it from me!
He parcels out our fields to a renegade.’”|Keeps the lament's pronoun shifts and difficult renegade rather than silently naming invaders.
2:5|So you will have no one to stretch a measuring line\nfor an allotted share in the LORD’s assembly.|Preserves land-allotment mechanism and communal exclusion.

2:6|“Do not pour out such words!” they pour out.\n“They must not speak about these things;\ndisgrace will not overtake us.”|Retains speech's dripping metaphor and marks a plausible opponent quotation while noting uncertain speaker boundaries.

2:7|Should the house of Jacob say,
“Has the LORD’s patience run short?
Are these his deeds?”
“Do not my words do good
to the one who walks uprightly?|Separates objection and divine response while keeping spirit/patience sense explicit in note.

2:8|But lately my people have risen like an enemy.
You strip the fine cloak off the garment
of those who pass by unsuspecting,
returning from war.|Follows the difficult garment layering and returned-war reading, without substituting peaceful civilians exclusively.

2:9|You drive the women of my people\nfrom the homes they cherish;\nyou take my splendor from their young children forever.|Preserves female victims, children, and divine splendor rather than generalizing displacement.
2:10|Get up and go! This is no resting place.\nBecause it is unclean, it brings destruction—\ngrievous destruction.|Keeps the difficult causal uncleanness and repeated ruin.

2:11|If someone trafficking in wind and falsehood lied,\n‘I will pour out words for you about wine and strong drink,’\nhe would be the preacher for this people!|Retains wind/falsehood and ironic welcome for alcohol-promising prophecy.

2:12|I will surely gather all of you, Jacob;
I will surely assemble Israel’s remnant.
I will bring them together like sheep in an enclosure,
like a flock in its pasture,
a noisy throng of people.|Retains emphatic gathering and flock noise; enclosure versus Bozrah noted.

2:13|The one who breaks through goes up before them.
They break through, pass the gate, and go out through it.
Their king passes before them,
with the LORD at their head.”|Keeps breakthrough repetitions and king/LORD relationship without supplying an identity beyond the text.

3:1|I said:
“Listen, heads of Jacob
and rulers of the house of Israel!
Should you not know justice?|Preserves prophetic first-person opening and leaders' responsibility to know justice.
3:2|You hate good and love evil.\nYou tear the skin from my people\nand the flesh from their bones.|Makes the victims clear from next verse while retaining the graphic butchery metaphor.

3:3|You eat my people’s flesh,
strip off their skin,
break their bones,
and chop them up like meat for a pot,
like flesh in a cauldron.”|Preserves every violent action rather than paraphrasing exploitation.

3:4|Then they will cry to the LORD,
but he will not answer them.
He will hide his face from them at that time
because their deeds have been evil.|Keeps reciprocal nonresponse and hidden face with stated cause.

3:5|This is what the LORD says about the prophets
who lead my people astray:
“When they have something between their teeth, they proclaim peace;
against anyone who puts nothing in their mouths,
they consecrate war.|Retains mouth/teeth economy and the contrast of peace versus consecrated war.

3:6|So night will come upon you without vision,
darkness without divination.
The sun will set on the prophets;
the day will grow dark over them.|Keeps loss of revelation expressed through four darkness clauses.

3:7|The seers will be ashamed
and the diviners disgraced.
They will all cover their upper lips,
for there is no answer from God.”|Retains the physical mourning/shame gesture and lack of divine answer.

3:8|But I am filled with power,
with the Spirit of the LORD, with justice and courage,
to declare Jacob’s rebellion to him
and Israel’s sin.|Preserves the prophet's contrasting commission and all enabling qualities.

3:9|Hear this, heads of the house of Jacob
and rulers of the house of Israel,
you who detest justice
and twist everything that is straight,|Repeats the leadership summons and straight/crooked contrast.
3:10|who build Zion with bloodshed\nand Jerusalem with injustice.|Keeps the city-building accusation and synonymous place pairing.

3:11|Her heads judge for bribes,
her priests teach for a price,
and her prophets divine for silver.
Yet they lean on the LORD and say,
“Is not the LORD among us? No disaster will reach us.”|Preserves all three corrupt roles and the claim of immunity as their speech.

3:12|So because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field,\nJerusalem will become heaps of rubble,\nand the temple mountain wooded heights.|Keeps direct responsibility and all three landscape reversals before chapter4's restoration.

4:1|In the days to come,
the mountain of the LORD’s house
will stand established above the mountains,
raised higher than the hills.
Peoples will stream toward it.|Preserves future mountain elevation and upward-streaming image.

4:2|Many nations will come and say,
“Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD,
to the house of Jacob’s God.
He will teach us his ways,
and we will walk in his paths.”
For instruction will go out from Zion,
and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.|Keeps nations' active invitation, teaching/walking, and both divine-name occurrences.

4:3|He will judge between many peoples
and settle disputes for powerful nations far away.
They will beat their swords into plowshares
and their spears into pruning hooks.
Nation will not raise a sword against nation,
and they will no longer learn war.|Preserves the range of nations and weapon transformations, with exact inverse relation to Joel3:10.

4:4|Each will sit beneath his own vine and fig tree,\nwith no one to frighten them,\nfor the mouth of the LORD of Armies has spoken.|Retains household agricultural security and divine mouth assurance.

4:5|All the peoples walk,
each in the name of its god;
but we will walk in the name of the LORD our God
forever and ever.|Keeps the plural nations' present conduct alongside communal resolve without doctrinal expansion.

4:6|“On that day,” declares the LORD,
“I will gather the lame
and assemble those driven away,
those whom I have afflicted.|Preserves marginalized groups and direct admission of divine affliction.

4:7|I will make the lame a remnant
and those cast far off a powerful nation.
The LORD will reign over them on Mount Zion
from now and forever.|Keeps reversal from weakness to nation and third-person divine name within speech.

4:8|And you, tower of the flock,
stronghold of daughter Zion—
to you the former dominion will come,
the kingship of daughter Jerusalem.”|Retains tower/stronghold and both daughter designations without fixing the site.
4:9|Now why do you cry aloud?\nHave you no king? Has your counselor perished,\nthat pain grips you like a woman in labor?|Keeps unanswered questions and labor comparison as the bridge to exile.

4:10|Writhe and push, daughter Zion, like a woman giving birth.
Now you must leave the city, live in the open country,
and go as far as Babylon.
There you will be rescued;
there the LORD will redeem you from your enemies’ hands.|Preserves Babylon and twice there, locating rescue in the place of exile.
4:11|Now many nations have gathered against you, saying,\n“Let her be defiled! Let our eyes feast on Zion!”|Keeps enemy words and their predatory gaze.
4:12|But they do not know the LORD’s thoughts\nor understand his counsel:\nhe has gathered them like sheaves to a threshing floor.|Retains their gathering reinterpreted as divine harvest preparation.

4:13|“Rise and thresh, daughter Zion!
I will make your horn iron and your hooves bronze,
and you will crush many peoples.
I will devote their gain to the LORD,
their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.”|Preserves metal animal imagery and pinned first-person I will devote, not silently you.

5:1|Now muster your troops, daughter of troops!\nA siege is laid against us.\nWith a rod they strike Israel’s judge on the cheek.|Retains troop/daughter wordplay and judge/rod humiliation; cutting oneself alternative noted.

5:2|But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah,
small among Judah’s clans,
from you will come forth for me
one who is to rule in Israel,
whose origins are from long ago, from ancient days.|Preserves smallness, divine for me, and temporal range without settling preexistence versus ancestral origins in text.

5:3|So he will give them up
until the woman in labor has given birth.
Then the rest of his brothers
will return to the people of Israel.|Keeps unnamed he and mother, and male kinship brothers without inserting later identities.

5:4|He will stand and shepherd
in the strength of the LORD,
in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God.
They will dwell securely,
for now he will be great to the ends of the earth.|Retains two name occurrences, shepherd ruler, and expanded reach.

5:5|And he will be peace.
When Assyria enters our land
and treads through our citadels,
we will raise against him seven shepherds,
eight leaders of men.|Keeps peace as predicate and seven/eight escalation rather than exact roster speculation.

5:6|They will shepherd the land of Assyria with the sword,
the land of Nimrod at its entrances.
He will rescue us from Assyria
when it enters our land and treads within our borders.|Preserves pointed entrances, sword shepherding, and plural-to-singular agency.

5:7|Then Jacob’s remnant among many peoples
will be like dew from the LORD,
like showers on grass,
which do not wait for a person
or depend on human beings.|Keeps the dew's independence and the remnant's position among peoples.

5:8|Jacob’s remnant among the nations, among many peoples,
will be like a lion among forest animals,
like a young lion among flocks of sheep,
which passes through, tramples, and tears,
with no one to rescue.|Retains the severe predator counterpart to the preceding dew image.
5:9|Your hand will rise over your adversaries,\nand all your enemies will be cut off.|Keeps lifted-hand victory and complete stated enemy loss.
5:10|“On that day,” declares the LORD,\n“I will cut off your horses from among you\nand destroy your chariots.|Preserves removal of the addressed people's military means, not merely enemy weapons.
5:11|I will cut off the cities of your land\nand tear down all your fortresses.|Retains both cities and fortresses rather than making one explanatory of the other.
5:12|I will cut off sorceries from your hands,\nand you will have no more fortune-tellers.|Keeps the repeated cut-off and distinction practice/practitioner.
5:13|I will cut off your carved images and sacred pillars from among you.\nYou will no longer bow down to the work of your hands.|Retains both objects and handmade-worship critique.
5:14|I will uproot your Asherah poles from among you\nand destroy your cities.|Follows pinned cities rather than emending to idols and retains named cult objects.
5:15|In anger and fury I will take vengeance\non the nations that have not listened.”|Keeps the concluding shift to nations and refusal to listen without adding a specified command.
6:1|Hear what the LORD says:\n“Rise, present your case before the mountains,\nand let the hills hear your voice.”|Preserves legal speech and mountains as hearing witnesses.

6:2|Hear the LORD’s case, mountains,
you enduring foundations of the earth!
The LORD has a case against his people;
he will dispute with Israel.|Keeps both name occurrences and repeated case to establish courtroom form.
6:3|“My people, what have I done to you?\nHow have I wearied you? Answer me!|Retains intimate address and open questions rather than supplying a charge.

6:4|I brought you up from the land of Egypt\nand redeemed you from the house of slavery.\nI sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam ahead of you.|Preserves slavery, redemption, and all three named leaders including Miriam.

6:5|My people, remember what Balak king of Moab planned
and what Balaam son of Beor answered him.
Remember the journey from Shittim to Gilgal,
so you may know the LORD’s righteous acts.”|Supplies remember journey for the elliptical place pair while retaining all names and righteousness language.

6:6|With what shall I approach the LORD
and bow before God on high?
Shall I approach him with burnt offerings,
with year-old calves?|Marks the responding questioner's voice and keeps exact age and offering type.

6:7|Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams,
with tens of thousands of rivers of oil?
Shall I give my firstborn for my rebellion,
the fruit of my body for the sin of my life?|Preserves extravagant quantities and disturbing child-sacrifice question as a question, not instruction.

6:8|He has told you, human being, what is good.
What does the LORD ask of you
but to do justice, love faithful kindness,
and walk humbly with your God?|Keeps universal adam, hesed's loyal kindness, and three distinct actions without doctrinal expansion.

6:9|The voice of the LORD calls to the city—\nwisdom sees your name:\n“Hear the rod and the one who appointed it!|Follows pinned sees/name rather than silently emending to fear/name; flags this very difficult line.
6:10|Are there still treasures gained by wickedness in the wicked house,\nand the accursed, undersized ephah?|Keeps economic specificity and uncertain opening syntax as a question.
6:11|Can I be pure with wicked scales\nand a pouch of fraudulent weights?|Preserves first-person pure wording rather than silently changing to acquit someone else.
6:12|The city’s rich are full of violence;\nher inhabitants speak lies,\nand deceit is on their tongues.|Keeps violence and deceit as separate charges and city personification.
6:13|So I too have made you sick with my blows,\ndevastating you because of your sins.|Preserves disease/striking sense rather than silently repointing to began.
6:15|You will sow but not reap;\nyou will tread olives but not anoint yourself with oil,\ntread grapes but not drink wine.|Preserves three labor/enjoyment reversals with olive and grape processing.

6:16|You have kept Omri’s decrees
and all the practices of Ahab’s house;
you have walked in their counsels.
So I will make you a desolation,
your inhabitants an object of hissing,
and you will bear my people’s disgrace.”|Retains both dynastic names and pinned my people rather than nations alternative.

7:1|Woe is me!
I am like someone after the summer fruit has been gathered,
after the vineyard has been gleaned:
no cluster to eat,
none of the first-ripe figs I crave.|Makes the harvest-afterward comparison natural while retaining both missing fruits.

7:3|Their hands are skilled at evil.
The ruler demands, the judge takes payment,
and the great man declares his own desire;
together they weave it into a scheme.|Keeps three corrupt participants and weaving metaphor rather than generic corruption.

7:4|The best of them is like a brier,
the most upright worse than a thorn hedge.
The day your watchmen announced, your reckoning, has come.
Now comes their confusion.|Retains thorn comparison and source pronoun shifts in the day announcement.

7:5|Do not trust a neighbor
or put confidence in a friend.
Guard the doors of your mouth
even from the woman who lies in your embrace.|Preserves intimate female relationship and mouth-door image in the social-collapse lament.

7:6|A son treats his father with contempt;
a daughter rises against her mother,
a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
A person’s enemies are the members of his own household.|Keeps every gendered kinship pair and the closing household generalization.
7:7|But I will watch for the LORD;\nI will wait for the God who saves me.\nMy God will hear me.|Retains watch/wait/hear progression and first-person resolve.

7:8|Do not rejoice over me, my enemy.\nThough I have fallen, I will rise.\nThough I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light.|Preserves the feminine enemy context in notes and the fall/rise dark/light pairs.

7:9|I will bear the LORD’s indignation
because I have sinned against him,
until he pleads my case and secures justice for me.
He will bring me into the light;
I will see his righteousness.|Keeps confession alongside hope for legal vindication, without erasing either.

7:10|My enemy will see, and shame will cover her,
she who said to me, ‘Where is the LORD your God?’
My eyes will look upon her;
now she will be trampled like mud in the streets.|Preserves female enemy, quoted taunt, and violent reversal.
7:11|A day for rebuilding your walls!\nOn that day the boundary will be pushed far out.|Chooses boundary for hoq while noting decree alternative; retains promise's terse form.
7:13|Yet the earth will become desolate because of its inhabitants,\nas the fruit of their deeds.|Retains the counterpoint of judgment beside restoration and fruit metaphor.

7:14|Shepherd your people with your staff,
the flock that is your inheritance,
living alone in woodland amid fruitful land.
Let them pasture in Bashan and Gilead as in ancient days.|Keeps pastoral petition, solitary woodland setting, and both fertile regions.
7:15|“As in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt,\nI will show him wonders.”|Preserves difficult you/him shift rather than silently normalizing the pronouns.

7:16|Nations will see and be ashamed despite all their might.\nThey will put a hand over their mouths;\ntheir ears will become deaf.|Keeps humbled military strength and bodily speech/hearing responses.

7:17|They will lick dust like a snake;
like creatures crawling on the ground,
they will come trembling from their strongholds.
They will turn in dread to the LORD our God
and be afraid of you.|Preserves snake/dust abasement and shift to divine direct address.

7:18|Who is a God like you,
forgiving guilt and passing over rebellion
for the remnant of his inheritance?
He does not hold on to anger forever,
because he delights in faithful love.|Keeps the name-echo question and you/his/he shifts with the remnant qualification.

7:19|He will again have compassion on us;\nhe will trample our guilt underfoot.\nYou will throw all their sins into the depths of the sea.|Preserves pinned our/their shift and concrete trampling and throwing images.

7:20|You will show faithfulness to Jacob\nand faithful love to Abraham,\nas you swore to our ancestors in days long ago.|Keeps paired ancestors and distinct emet/hesed terms, linking conclusion to enduring oath.
